title: Prefill/Decode lane scheduler with kernel smoothing and speculative KV hedging
author: Leah Park
description:
Motivation: interactive workloads show bimodal request shapes (short-turn chat vs long generation) which causes resource interference in the prefill->decode pipeline. Small/latency-sensitive requests stall behind large prefill kernels or large KV priming windows, increasing tail latency. This change introduces a lightweight lane scheduler that separates requests into short and long lanes, applies kernel smoothing to reduce variance in GPU kernel invocation times, and adds a speculative KV hedging slot for short-lane requests to opportunistically warm KV cache without impacting long-lane throughput.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a PrefillDecodeLaneScheduler that classifies requests at admission time into SHORT and LONG lanes based on token budget and historical service times. The scheduler enforces adaptive concurrency caps per lane and provides a fast-path for SHORT lane prefill (micro-chunking with prioritized KV micro-warmups). 2) Introduces KernelSmoother: a small runtime shim that aggregates small kernel launches into time-aligned waves to avoid high-frequency micro-kernel variance on A100/RTX instances. The smoother keeps latency SLOs for SHORT lane by dispatching at low-latency thresholds and amortizes overhead for LONG lane heavy prefill. 3) Implements a SpeculativeKVHedger: a guarded speculative prefetch that consumes a small token budget to prefetch likely KV entries for SHORT lane requests when GPU occupancy permits; hedging is no-op when cache pressure is high. 4) Runtime metrics and tracing hooks: per-lane p50/p95/p99, kernel-invocation variance, kv-hedge-hit-rate, admission-rejects. 5) Integration tests and perf benchmark harness extension to simulate mixed workload traffic profiles.

Design notes and trade-offs: - Classification uses an exponentially-weighted moving average of request service time and an explicit token limit heuristic to keep rules simple and deterministic. This avoids a full ML classifier in the hot path. - KernelSmoother adds small queuing (micro- to single-digit-ms) deliberate delay to reduce tail jitter; configurable via runtime flags and adaptive policy. - Speculative hedging is conservative: each worker has a per-second hedge budget to prevent KV eviction storms. Hedging disabled under kv_pressure > 0.75. - This is primarily a scheduling and runtime shim; no model changes required.

Testing & results: synthetic mixed-profile load (50% short chat 8-24 tokens, 50% long gen 512-1024 tokens) on a 4xA100 dedicated pool: - Baseline (main): short-lane p99 = 410ms, long-lane throughput = 820 samples/s - This PR: short-lane p99 = 260ms (-36%), long-lane throughput = 790 samples/s (-3.7%), overall GPU utilization improved 6% due to reduced kernel tail collisions. KV hedge hit-rate ~12% on short lane; when hedging budget increased we saw diminishing returns and slightly higher eviction churn.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation + unit tests for lane scheduler - [x] KernelSmoother runtime shim + tests - [x] SpeculativeKVHedger + integration tests - [x] Bench harness extension and perf artifacts uploaded - [x] Documentation (runtime flags, observability)

Related Linear items: ENG-1429, ENG-2034. Related PRs: none required but this complements earlier kernel coalescing work.
